```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)

# Helpers identicos aos restantes relatorios do projeto (mesma convencao visual)
report_table <- function(x, max_col_width_cm = NULL, font_size = 9) {
  ft <- flextable::flextable(x) |>
    flextable::theme_box() |>
    flextable::bg(part = "header", bg = "gray85") |>
    flextable::bold(part = "header") |>
    flextable::fontsize(size = font_size, part = "header") |>
    flextable::fontsize(size = font_size, part = "body") |>
    flextable::align(align = "center", part = "header") |>
    flextable::valign(valign = "center", part = "all") |>
    flextable::autofit()
  if (!is.null(max_col_width_cm)) {
    widths_in <- dim(ft)$widths
    ft <- flextable::width(ft, j = seq_along(widths_in), width = pmin(widths_in * 2.54, max_col_width_cm), unit = "cm")
  }
  ft
}

pv <- function(x, default = "not available") if (is.null(x) || length(x) == 0L || all(is.na(x)) || identical(x, "")) default else paste(x, collapse = ", ")

# Numeros: 1 casa decimal; NA -> "Not available" (nunca 0)
fmt_pct <- function(v) ifelse(is.na(v), "Not available", sprintf("%.1f", v))
fmt_coverage <- function(v) ifelse(is.na(v), "-", sprintf("%.1f", v))
fmt_txt <- function(v, empty = "-") ifelse(is.na(v) | !nzchar(as.character(v)), empty, as.character(v))

# Um paragrafo em branco entre blocos texto/tabela/figura
fmt_p <- function(v) ifelse(is.na(v), "-", ifelse(v < 0.001, "<0.001", sprintf("%.3f", v)))

gap <- function() cat("\n\n&nbsp;\n\n")

show_table <- function(df, max_col_width_cm = 3, font_size = 9) {
  if (is.null(df) || nrow(df) == 0L) {
    cat("None.\n\n")
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }
  cat(knitr::knit_print(report_table(df, max_col_width_cm = max_col_width_cm, font_size = font_size)))
  invisible(NULL)
}

show_plot <- function(fig) {
  f <- tempfile(fileext = ".png")
  ggplot2::ggsave(f, fig$p, width = 6.3, height = fig$h, dpi = 220)
  cat(sprintf("\n\n![](%s)\n\n", normalizePath(f, winslash = "/")))
}
```

**`r params$project_ref`** -- IDF Availability Report -- Turbine(s): **`r params$turbines_text`**

Analysis period: **`r params$period_start`** to **`r params$period_end`**

Analysis date: `r params$analysis_date` | Responsible Team: `r params$username` | Code version: `r params$code_version`

This report is descriptive and fully automated, generated end-to-end by an R code pipeline.

**Technical Summary**

```{r summary-text, results='asis'}
cat(sprintf(
  "%d turbine(s) (%s) and %d IDF units (%d primary, %d secondary) were analysed from %s to %s; the turbine-IDF relation comes from: %s.\n\n",
  params$n_turbines, params$turbines_text, params$n_units, params$n_primary, params$n_secondary,
  params$period_start, params$period_end, params$relation_sources
))
x <- params$net_overall
if (!is.null(x) && nrow(x) > 0L) {
  cat(sprintf(
    "Across all evaluated units, raw offline time was %s%% of daylight time, net / confirmed offline time %s%% and time with no evidence %s%%.\n\n",
    fmt_pct(x$raw_offline_pct[1]), fmt_pct(x$net_offline_pct[1]), fmt_pct(x$no_evidence_pct[1])
  ))
}
n_alert <- if (is.null(params$alert_table)) 0L else nrow(params$alert_table)
n_turb <- if (is.null(params$turbine_alert_table)) 0L else nrow(params$turbine_alert_table)
cat(sprintf(
  "%d IDF unit(s) are listed in the persistent-failure alert (offline for more than %s%% of the daylight time of the period, or without heartbeat records); %d turbine(s) have no IDF unit outside the alert.\n",
  n_alert, params$persistent_failure_threshold_pct, n_turb
))
```

---

# Scope and method

Each IDF unit is analysed for the turbines it protects. The primary unit of a turbine is the one with the largest overlap between the detection buffer of the unit and that of the turbine; the other units overlapping `r if (params$relation_min_pct_coverage > 0) paste0("at least ", params$relation_min_pct_coverage, "%") else "any part"` of the turbine buffer are secondary, tertiary, ... units in decreasing order of coverage`r if (is.finite(params$relation_max_secondary)) paste0(" (at most ", params$relation_max_secondary, " per turbine)") else ""`, unless a manual turbine-IDF matrix defines them. The buffer radius is `r params$idf_op_detection_range` m. Unit names are the full IDF unit names reported in the heartbeat files.

Each IDF unit sends a heartbeat approximately every `r params$heartbeat_interval_min` minutes when operational; a unit is considered offline once `r params$heartbeat_offline_gap_min` minutes pass without a heartbeat, counting only daylight hours (sunrise to sunset, computed from the project coordinates). Every offline interval is then classified by the evidence available for the same period:

```{r comm-failure-def, results='asis'}
if (isFALSE(params$attribution_by_unit)) {
  cat("- **IDF unit communication failure**: no heartbeat, but a curtailment was triggered during the gap at one of the turbines the unit protects (any IDF unit; curtailments are not attributed to individual units in this run) -- the system was actively deciding/acting, so the missing heartbeat may reflect a communication fault rather than bird protection being off.\n")
} else {
  cat("- **IDF unit communication failure**: no heartbeat, but a curtailment was triggered during the gap by a bird track recorded by this same IDF unit at one of the turbines it protects -- the unit was actively deciding/acting, so the missing heartbeat reflects a communication fault rather than bird protection being off.\n")
}
```
- **Turbine operational, no detection**: no heartbeat and no such curtailment, but SCADA still recorded RPM readings from a turbine the unit protects.
- **No evidence (heartbeat and SCADA both missing)**: neither signal is available; requires manual review.

**Raw offline** is the share of daylight time without heartbeat; **net / confirmed offline** is raw offline minus the minutes classified as communication failure; **no evidence** is already included in the net figure and shown separately because it needs manual review. Time before the first and after the last heartbeat of a unit within the period counts as offline, like any other gap. A unit that received no heartbeat at all during the period, but appears in the heartbeat records of other periods while other units did report, is therefore **100% offline** ("Heartbeats (n)" = 0): the missing signal is the finding. Only a unit that does not appear in the heartbeat records at all (for example because its code does not match) is shown as "Not available" / "Not evaluated", since no assessment is possible for it.

# Turbine and IDF unit relation

```{r relation-table, results='asis'}
x <- params$relation_table
if (!is.null(x) && nrow(x) > 0L) {
  d <- data.frame(
    Turbine = x$turbine, Role = x$role, `IDF Unit` = x$unit,
    `Coverage (%)` = ifelse(is.na(x$pct_coverage), "-", sprintf("%.1f", x$pct_coverage)),
    Source = x$relation_source,
    `Offline (%)` = fmt_pct(x$offline_pct), Category = fmt_txt(x$availability_cat),
    check.names = FALSE
  )
  show_table(d, max_col_width_cm = 3)
} else cat("No turbine-IDF relation could be established.\n\n")
```

## Coverage without the primary IDF unit

Geometric estimate of the protection that remains when the primary IDF unit of a turbine fails: share of the circular area of radius `r params$turbine_area_radius_m` m around the turbine that is covered by the detection buffer (`r params$idf_op_detection_range` m) of the other units of the relation -- secondary, tertiary and so on, taken together (the union of their buffers, so overlapping areas are counted once). "Primary" is the share covered by the primary unit alone and "All units" the share covered by all units together.

```{r remaining-table, results='asis'}
x <- params$remaining_table
gap()
if (!is.null(x) && nrow(x) > 0L) {
  d <- data.frame(
    Turbine = x$turbine, `Primary unit` = fmt_txt(x$primary_unit), `Other units` = fmt_txt(x$other_units),
    `Other units (n)` = x$n_other_units,
    `Primary (%)` = fmt_coverage(x$primary_pct),
    `Without primary (%)` = fmt_coverage(x$without_primary_pct),
    `All units (%)` = fmt_coverage(x$all_units_pct),
    check.names = FALSE
  )
  show_table(d, max_col_width_cm = 3.2, font_size = 8)
} else cat("No coverage could be computed.\n\n")
```

# Curtailments triggered by each IDF unit

Curtailments of each turbine triggered by `r if (nzchar(params$species_of_interest)) params$species_of_interest else "any species"` during the analysed period, by the IDF unit that triggered them, for the IDF units that contribute to the turbine (the units of its relation). Each curtailment is attributed to the IDF unit that recorded the bird track that triggered it (the unit of the track point closest in time to the start of the curtailment). The track data are retrieved for the units that contribute to the turbines only, so curtailments whose track is not available, or that were triggered by a unit outside the relation, are not interpreted: they are only counted below each table. "%" is the share of the curtailments attributed to the units listed. Together with the offline time of each unit in the same period, the table shows whether curtailments keep being triggered by the other units while the primary unit is offline.

Units are listed by decreasing coverage of the turbine: the unit with the largest coverage is the **Primary** unit, followed by **Secondary**, **Tertiary**, 4th, 5th and so on.

```{r curtl-by-unit-table, results='asis'}
x <- params$curtl_by_unit_table
gap()
if (!is.null(x) && nrow(x) > 0L) {
  ord_lab <- c("Primary", "Secondary", "Tertiary", paste0(4:30, "th"))
  d <- data.frame(
    Turbine = x$turbine, `IDF Unit` = x$unit,
    `Coverage rank` = ifelse(is.na(x$rank), "-", ord_lab[pmin(x$rank, length(ord_lab))]),
    `Coverage (%)` = fmt_coverage(x$pct_coverage),
    `Offline (%)` = fmt_pct(x$offline_pct),
    Curtailments = x$n, `%` = ifelse(is.na(x$pct), "-", sprintf("%.1f", x$pct)),
    check.names = FALSE
  )
  show_table(d, max_col_width_cm = 2.8, font_size = 8)
  t <- params$curtl_totals_table
  if (!is.null(t) && nrow(t) > 0L) {
    gap()
    for (i in seq_len(nrow(t))) {
      cat(sprintf("Turbine %s: %d curtailment(s) in the period; %d attributed to the units above, %d attributed to other units and %d without track data (not shown).\n\n",
                  t$turbine[i], t$n_total[i], t$n_in_relation[i], t$n_other_units[i], t$n_no_track[i]))
    }
  }
} else cat("Curtailments by IDF unit are not available for this run: the attribution of curtailments to units needs the track data (attribute_curtailments_by_unit = TRUE).\n\n")
```

# Offline evidence calendars

Every daylight time slot of the period for each IDF unit, laid out as a calendar (date on the horizontal axis, time of day on the vertical axis); units are grouped in figures and shown in the order of the relation table above. Each slot is coloured by one of six statuses:

- **Online**: a heartbeat was received for this slot.
- **IDF unit communication failure**: no heartbeat, but a curtailment was triggered during the gap by a bird track recorded by this same IDF unit at one of the turbines it protects -- the unit was actively deciding/acting, so the missing heartbeat reflects a communication fault rather than bird protection being off.
- **Turbine operational, no detection**: no heartbeat and no such curtailment, but SCADA still recorded RPM readings from a turbine the unit protects -- mechanically operational, simply with no bird triggering a response.
- **No evidence (heartbeat and SCADA both missing)**: neither signal is available for this slot; requires manual review, since it can reflect a genuine gap in bird-protection coverage or a data gap affecting heartbeat and SCADA at the same time.
- **Night**: outside daylight hours, when bird protection is not evaluated.
- **No data**: no underlying data available for this slot, independent of the evidence check above (in this report, a unit that does not appear in the heartbeat records at all, so it cannot be evaluated).

```{r calendars, results='asis'}
figs <- params$calendar_figures
if (is.null(figs) || length(figs) == 0L) {
  cat("No IDF units to display.\n\n")
} else {
  for (fig in figs) {
    gap()
    show_plot(fig)
  }
}
```

# Malfunctions reported by the IDF team

```{r malf-intro, results='asis'}
x <- params$malfunction_events
if (is.null(x) || nrow(x) == 0L) {
  cat("No malfunctions reported by the IDF team were provided for this report.\n\n")
} else {
  cat("The IDF team reported the malfunctions below. They are not directly available in, or computable from, the portal data (heartbeats, SCADA, curtailments). For WFOV camera malfunctions, the tracks recorded by the unit are compared before and after the reported date; the other types are listed without assessment.\n\n")
  gap()
  show_table(as.data.frame(x), max_col_width_cm = 5)
}
```

```{r wfov-method, results='asis'}
if (length(params$wfov_results) > 0L) {
  cat("\n\n**WFOV camera pattern.** The WFOV module is the set of eight monocular cameras that make the first detection of objects in the visible space; the objects are then followed by the binocular stereo camera. Every track in the TrackReport records the WFOV camera that captured it. For each reported WFOV malfunction, the share of the tracks of the unit captured by each camera is compared between the window before and the window after the reported date and time. A camera that stopped capturing objects shows as a share that falls to, or close to, zero. The windows are counted from the reported date and time and each track is counted once per camera (at its first record). Significance is assessed with a Monte Carlo permutation test: the window blocks (`r pv(params$wfov_block_hours)` h each, aligned with the reported time) are randomly re-labelled \"before\" or 'after' `r pv(params$wfov_n_perm)` times, keeping the number of blocks of each window, and the change in the share of every camera is recomputed. Blocks, not single tracks, are permuted because tracks that are close in time (the same flock, the same hour) are not independent. The p-value of a camera is the proportion of permutations with a change at least as large as the observed one (in absolute value); the adjusted p-value compares it with the largest change among all cameras in each permutation, so it accounts for looking at eight cameras at once. The overall p-value is the adjusted p-value of the camera with the largest change. All are descriptive and depend on the number of tracks and on the random seed (the Monte Carlo error is about 0.005 near p = 0.05). When an earlier period is configured, it covers the days before the 'before' window, in the same unit and therefore in the same airspace. Comparing the earlier period with the 'before' window (no failure) shows how much the unit varies by itself from one period to the next: a change after the reported date that is not larger than this natural change is not evidence of a failure. The report gives the same tests for the earlier period against the 'before' window, for the earlier period and the 'before' window pooled against the 'after' window (a longer baseline), and for the number of tracks of the unit. The camera shares compare the composition of the tracks of the unit and do not show a change in their number. The number of tracks of a unit depends on the bird activity, which is not known: a lower number of tracks after the reported date can reflect the unit or fewer birds. For this reason the change of the unit is compared with a benchmark, the same ratio (tracks per day after / before) in neighbouring IDF units that operated normally in the same period (heartbeats complete in the whole window); the benchmark units are listed for each event. The relative change versus the benchmark is the ratio of the unit divided by the ratio of the pooled benchmark units, and its p-value uses the same block permutation, with the same blocks re-labelled for the unit and for the benchmark so that the activity common to the birds is kept. The benchmark is not a control in the experimental sense: neighbouring units see different parts of the airspace, so the individual ratios of the benchmark units show how much the ratio varies between units that did not fail. The reported date may be earlier than the date of the record, and a change in the bird traffic of the period alone can change the shares. The comparison complements, and does not replace, the heartbeat, SCADA and curtailment evidence in the previous sections.\n\n")
}
```

```{r wfov-events, results='asis'}
for (r in params$wfov_results) {
  cat(sprintf("\n\n## %s -- %s\n\n", r$label, r$type))
  cat(sprintf("Reported date and time: %s. Windows: %s days before and %s days after%s.\n\n", r$event_time, r$days_before, r$days_after,
              if (isTRUE(r$has_pre)) sprintf(", plus an earlier period of %s days before the \"before\" window", r$days_pre) else ""))
  if (nzchar(r$note)) cat(r$note, "\n\n")
  x <- r$totals
  if (!is.null(x) && nrow(x) > 0L) {
    gap()
    d <- data.frame(Window = x$period, From = format(x$from, "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M"), To = format(x$to, "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M"),
                    `Tracks (n)` = x$tracks, `Tracks per day` = sprintf("%.1f", x$tracks_per_day),
                    `Active cameras (n)` = x$cameras_active,
                    `Ratio vs previous window` = if ("ratio_vs_previous" %in% names(x)) ifelse(is.na(x$ratio_vs_previous), "-", sprintf("%.2f", x$ratio_vs_previous)) else "-",
                    `p (perm.)` = if ("p_vs_previous" %in% names(x)) fmt_p(x$p_vs_previous) else "-", check.names = FALSE)
    show_table(d, max_col_width_cm = 4)
  }
  bm <- r$benchmark
  if (!is.null(bm)) {
    t <- bm$total
    cat(sprintf("\n\n**Benchmark.** %d reference unit(s)%s. Tracks per day after / before: %s for the unit and %s for the pooled benchmark; the unit changed %s%% relative to the benchmark (permutation p = %s).\n\n",
      nrow(bm$refs), if (isTRUE(bm$manual)) " (chosen manually)" else " (nearest units with complete heartbeats in the window)",
      ifelse(is.na(t$unit_ratio), "not available", sprintf("%.2f", t$unit_ratio)), ifelse(is.na(t$ref_ratio), "not available", sprintf("%.2f", t$ref_ratio)),
      ifelse(is.na(t$relative_vs_benchmark_pct), "not available", sprintf("%+.1f", t$relative_vs_benchmark_pct)), fmt_p(t$p_perm)))
    gap()
    d <- data.frame(`IDF Unit` = bm$refs$unit, `Distance (m)` = ifelse(is.na(bm$refs$dist_m), "-", sprintf("%.0f", bm$refs$dist_m)),
                    `Heartbeats complete (%)` = ifelse(is.na(bm$refs$completeness), "-", sprintf("%.0f", 100 * bm$refs$completeness)),
                    `Tracks before (n)` = bm$refs$tracks_before, `Tracks after (n)` = bm$refs$tracks_after,
                    `Ratio after / before` = ifelse(is.na(bm$refs$ratio), "-", sprintf("%.2f", bm$refs$ratio)), check.names = FALSE)
    show_table(d, max_col_width_cm = 4, font_size = 8)
    if (!is.null(r$fig_benchmark)) { gap(); show_plot(r$fig_benchmark) }
  } else if (isTRUE(r$n_benchmark_units == 0L)) {
    cat("\n\nNo benchmark could be computed: no neighbouring IDF unit had complete heartbeats in the whole window (or none was provided), so the change in the number of tracks cannot be separated from a change in the bird activity.\n\n")
  }
  x <- r$summary
  if (!is.null(x) && nrow(x) > 0L) {
    if (!is.null(r$omnibus) && !is.na(r$omnibus)) cat(sprintf("Overall permutation p-value (camera with the largest change, adjusted for the eight cameras): %s for before vs after%s.\n\n", fmt_p(r$omnibus),
      if (isTRUE(r$has_pre)) sprintf(", %s for earlier period vs before (no failure, natural variation of the unit) and %s for earlier period + before vs after", fmt_p(r$omnibus_placebo), fmt_p(r$omnibus_pooled)) else ""))
    gap()
    has_pre <- isTRUE(r$has_pre) && "delta_placebo_pp" %in% names(x)
    d <- data.frame(Camera = x$camera,
                    `Earlier (%)` = if (has_pre) fmt_pct(x$pct_pre) else "-",
                    `Before (n)` = x$n_before, `Before (%)` = fmt_pct(x$pct_before),
                    `After (n)` = x$n_after, `After (%)` = fmt_pct(x$pct_after),
                    `Change after-before (pp)` = ifelse(is.na(x$delta_pp), "-", sprintf("%+.1f", x$delta_pp)),
                    `Change before-earlier (pp)` = if (has_pre) ifelse(is.na(x$delta_placebo_pp), "-", sprintf("%+.1f", x$delta_placebo_pp)) else "-",
                    `p adj.` = fmt_p(x$p_adj),
                    `p adj. before vs earlier` = if (has_pre) fmt_p(x$p_adj_placebo) else "-",
                    `p adj. vs earlier + before` = if (has_pre) fmt_p(x$p_adj_pooled) else "-",
                    `Larger than before-earlier change` = if (has_pre) ifelse(x$exceeds_placebo, "Yes", "No") else "-",
                    `Tracks vs benchmark (%)` = if (!is.null(bm)) { v <- bm$by_camera$relative_vs_benchmark_pct[match(x$camera, bm$by_camera$camera)]; ifelse(is.na(v), "-", sprintf("%+.1f", v)) } else "-",
                    `p vs benchmark (adj.)` = if (!is.null(bm)) fmt_p(bm$by_camera$p_adj[match(x$camera, bm$by_camera$camera)]) else "-",
                    Status = x$status, check.names = FALSE)
    show_table(d, max_col_width_cm = 4, font_size = 8)
    if (!is.null(r$fig_share)) { gap(); show_plot(r$fig_share) }
    if (!is.null(r$fig_daily)) { gap(); show_plot(r$fig_daily) }
  } else if (!nzchar(r$note)) cat("No tracks of this unit were recorded in the comparison windows.\n\n")
  x <- r$context
  if (!is.null(x) && nrow(x) > 0L) {
    cat("\n\nOther evidence in the same windows (rates per day covered by each dataset; \"Not available\" when the dataset does not cover the window):\n\n")
    gap()
    d <- data.frame(Metric = x$metric, Before = fmt_pct(x$before), After = fmt_pct(x$after),
                    `Change (%)` = ifelse(is.na(x$change_pct), "-", sprintf("%+.1f", x$change_pct)), check.names = FALSE)
    show_table(d, max_col_width_cm = 8)
  }
}
```

# Alerts

## Persistent failure

IDF units offline for more than `r params$persistent_failure_threshold_pct`% of the daylight time of the analysed period (`r if (identical(params$persistent_failure_basis, "net")) "net / confirmed offline time" else "raw offline time"`), including units that received no heartbeat at all in the period, and units that cannot be evaluated because they do not appear in the heartbeat records.

```{r alert-table, results='asis'}
x <- params$alert_table
gap()
if (!is.null(x) && nrow(x) > 0L) {
  d <- data.frame(
    `IDF Unit` = x$unit, `Primary for` = fmt_txt(x$primary_for), `Secondary for` = fmt_txt(x$secondary_for),
    `Heartbeats (n)` = ifelse(is.na(x$n_heartbeats), "-", format(x$n_heartbeats, big.mark = ",")),
    `Offline (%)` = fmt_pct(x$offline_pct), `Net offline (%)` = fmt_pct(x$net_offline_pct),
    `No evidence (%)` = fmt_pct(x$no_evidence_pct), Status = x$status,
    check.names = FALSE
  )
  show_table(d, max_col_width_cm = 4, font_size = 8)
} else cat("No IDF unit met the persistent-failure criterion.\n\n")
```

## Turbines without an IDF unit outside the alert

Turbines for which every protecting unit (primary and secondary) is in the alert above.

```{r turbine-alert-table, results='asis'}
x <- params$turbine_alert_table
gap()
if (!is.null(x) && nrow(x) > 0L) {
  show_table(data.frame(Turbine = x$turbine, `Protecting IDF units` = x$units, `Units (n)` = x$n_units, check.names = FALSE), max_col_width_cm = 8)
} else cat("None.\n\n")
```

# Methodology, Definitions and Data Notes

This section states how each figure of the report is obtained, so that every number can be traced and read in context. It is descriptive: it reports what the data show and does not establish the cause of any failure.

**Data and period**

- All times are local time (`r pv(params$timezone_name)`). The analysed period is `r pv(params$period_start)` to `r pv(params$period_end)`, in calendar days of that time zone.
- Duplicate rows in the raw files are removed on loading.
- The period actually covered by each dataset, as available when the report was produced, is:

```{r annex-data-sources, results='asis'}
x <- params$data_sources
gap()
if (!is.null(x) && nrow(x) > 0L) {
  x <- as.data.frame(x); x[is.na(x)] <- "-"
  show_table(x, max_col_width_cm = 6)
} else cat("The data coverage table is not available for this run.\n\n")
```

- Data that are not part of the period retrieved are treated as unavailable, not as zero. Heartbeat files cover all IDF units of the wind farm for the period retrieved.
- Figures are rounded for display (1 decimal for percentages); percentages may not add up to exactly 100.

**Turbine and IDF unit relation**

- The detection buffer of each IDF unit and of each turbine has a radius of `r pv(params$idf_op_detection_range)` m. "Coverage (%)" is the part of the area of the turbine buffer that is inside the buffer of the IDF unit.
- Units are ranked by decreasing coverage: the largest is the primary unit of the turbine, then secondary, tertiary, 4th, 5th and so on, unless a manual turbine-IDF matrix defines the relation (source: `r pv(params$relation_sources)`). The ranking is geometric: it does not use bird detections and ignores terrain.
- "Coverage without the primary IDF unit" is the area of the circle of radius `r pv(params$turbine_area_radius_m)` m around the turbine covered by the union of all non-primary unit buffers, divided by the area of that circle.

**Offline time**

- A unit sends a heartbeat about every `r pv(params$heartbeat_interval_min)` minutes when operational. A gap of at least `r pv(params$heartbeat_offline_gap_min)` minutes without a heartbeat is an offline period.
- Only daylight hours (sunrise to sunset, computed from the project coordinates) are evaluated; night time is not counted as unavailability.
- The time between the start of the period and the first heartbeat of a unit, and between its last heartbeat and the end of the period, counts as offline like any other gap, within the period covered by the heartbeat data of all units. A unit without any heartbeat in a period covered by the data is 100% offline; a unit that does not appear in the heartbeat data at all is "Not evaluated".
- Net / confirmed offline time is the raw offline time minus the time classified as communication failure. "No evidence" time is not subtracted: it is included in the net figure and shown apart because it needs manual review.
- The evidence for each offline interval is the one listed in "Scope and method". Curtailments count as evidence only for the unit that recorded the track that triggered them; curtailments whose track is not in the track data are not evidence for any unit, so communication-failure time is a lower bound. SCADA readings are matched to the turbine, not to a unit.

**Curtailments per IDF unit**

- Only curtailments of the species of interest (`r pv(params$species_of_interest, "all species")`) that started inside the analysed period are counted, and only for the units that contribute to the turbine (primary and secondary). Curtailments triggered by other units, or with no track available, are counted apart and are not compared with the rest of the wind farm.
- The unit of a curtailment is the unit that recorded the track point closest in time to the start of the order. Tracks are read only for the curtailments of the period.

**Reported malfunctions (WFOV cameras)**

- Malfunctions come from the list supplied by the IDF team (unit, date and time, type) and are not derived from the portal data. Only WFOV malfunctions are assessed, through the WFOV camera recorded in each track of the unit: the share of tracks per camera before and after the reported date and time, within the windows stated for each event. The tracks are those of the TrackReport files provided, which must cover both windows; when they do not, the comparison is stated as partial.
- Earlier period: when configured, the days before the 'before' window are analysed in the same unit. The change between the earlier period and the 'before' window (no reported failure) is the natural variation of the unit, in the same airspace, and the change after the reported date is read against it. The earlier period and the 'before' window pooled are also compared with the 'after' window.
- Benchmark: neighbouring IDF units (the nearest ones with at least `r pv(round(100 * params$wfov_benchmark_min_completeness))`% of the expected heartbeats in the whole window, and without a reported malfunction of their own in the window) give the change in the number of tracks per day over the same period; the unit is compared with them through the ratio after / before. The result is relative: a fall that also occurs in the benchmark units is attributed to the bird activity. The per-camera figure compares the ratio of each camera of the unit with the ratio of the benchmark total, since the cameras of different units point to different sectors.
- The comparison is indirect evidence: it depends on the birds that crossed the area in each window, on the number of tracks (few tracks give unstable shares) and on the accuracy of the reported date.

**Alerts**

- A unit is in the persistent-failure alert when its `r if (identical(params$persistent_failure_basis, "net")) "net" else "raw"` offline time exceeds `r pv(params$persistent_failure_threshold_pct)`% of the daylight time of the period, or when it has no heartbeat records. A turbine is listed when every unit that protects it is in the alert.
- Offline time depends on the period chosen: a short period amplifies the weight of a single gap, and the contractual availability should be read for the contractual reference period.

**Sample size and interpretation**

- Counts of curtailments per unit are small: always read a percentage together with the count next to it.
- Every result is conditional on the data retrieved (period, units and datasets above). The report is generated automatically from those data, with the code version stated at the top of the report.

```{r annex, results='asis'}
if (nzchar(params$xlsx_name)) cat(sprintf("\n\n&nbsp;\n\n*The full tables are available in the accompanying workbook: `%s`.*\n", params$xlsx_name))
```
